<reason>Side B (PRO) won by owning the geometric reality of land scarcity and dismantling Side A's alternatives—showing lease-based systems violate the religious covenants A invoked, vertical structures remain finite, green burial still consumes scarce land, and cemetery expansion contradicts the land-scarce premise. While A mounted a strong religious freedom and equity defense, B's "generational lockout" argument proved decisive: A's plan inevitably locks out future families once dedicated sections fill, whereas B's circular memorials preserve public access indefinitely. B also exposed A's reliance on peri-urban cemeteries after attacking them as inequitable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Pressure Questions and Rebuttal 2 forcing A to confront that "dedicated sections" inevitably fill, exposing A's "policy choice" evasion (expanding cemeteries into housing/parks) as incompatible with land scarcity, while B demonstrated reusable, high-density memorials that avoid generational lockout.</best_rebuttal>
